requested_text: Chose “Mass Raid Prioritisation: Jets First, UAVs After, Unknowns Referred” from the list.

scenario_instance.scenario_name: Saturation Raid — Tight Wave Spacing, Referred Unknowns
scenario_instance.situation_brief:
You hold the console at a single fixed air-defence site. The radar does not rotate: it covers a 120-degree sector centred on 090 degrees (030 to 150) and you are blind behind it. Detection is class-dependent — fast jets out to about 150 km, rotary-wing to about 100 km, small unmanned air vehicles only inside 50 km, which means a UAV is already inside your medium ring the moment it appears. Radar tilt is yours to manage; anything flying under the tilt is neither tracked nor engageable until you move it.

Engagement rings are 70 km (long), 50 km (medium) and 20 km (short), with a 5 km inner limit. The system computes time to intercept and probability of kill for the selected track and recommends interceptor and launcher. There is a hard system limit of two rockets in the air at any moment; a third engagement cannot begin until one of the two resolves as hit, kill or miss. Your magazine is finite and the assessment counts rounds expended.

IFF interrogation is unavailable on this fit — there is no transponder reply on any track. Identification comes from system classification and from you. Tracks presented as Unknown are questions, not permissions: refer them to the commander, who answers in about fifteen seconds, and fire on nothing that is not classified Enemy.

A mass raid is developing in the sector. Multiple tracks of mixed class are inbound with overlapping arrivals, and the picture at zero is not the picture you will be fighting thirty seconds from now. You have 210 seconds. Sequence the queue, keep both launchers working, and be ready to justify what you chose not to shoot.

resources.name: Rockets simultaneously in flight (hard system limit)
Commander referral response time for an Unknown track

live_tracks.notes: Lead fast closer. Crosses the 70 km ring at roughly 21 s and is inside the short ring by the end of the window if unengaged.
Second fast closer, reaches the long-range ring around 43 s — while the first engagement is very likely still in flight.
High and fastest of the three; enters the long-range ring near 58 s, when the two-in-flight limit is most likely saturated.
First of the unmanned wave; appears already inside the medium ring and reads as the nearest track on the display.
Low-mid altitude; may be marginal against a badly set tilt.
Arrives with the tail of the jet wave still being serviced.
Fastest of the unmanned wave; northern edge of the sector.
Last hostile to appear, near the southern sector edge and low — easy to leave unserviced at the end of the run.

Never resolves unaided. Closing hard on the site with heading and altitude changes that read as an attack run; crosses the 70 km ring around 108 s, with the unmanned wave already stacked inside the medium ring. Classification must be referred to the commander; behaviour is not a classification.
Low and slow on the southern flank; may drop below the tilt and reappear, which can present as a new unresolved track. Correlates to an own-force call sign late in the run.
Appears inside the medium ring on a profile visually indistinguishable from the hostile unmanned wave. Resolves only in the last seconds of the window.

success_criteria.statement: Pass requires: all three fast closers engaged at the earliest valid firing solution the system offers and destroyed inside the window; the unmanned wave then worked as a continuous queue on next-available-valid-solution, with no more than two unmanned hostiles left unserviced at the end of the run; every Unknown track referred to the commander; and no round fired at any track not classified Enemy. Engaging an Unknown or a friendly is an outright fail regardless of hostiles destroyed. A leaked fast closer fails the run. Holding fire while both rockets are committed is correct behaviour, not inaction — breaking or retargeting a committed engagement is scored as an error even if the outcome is favourable. No more than eleven interceptors may be expended.
